newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks finish higher as techs sizzle again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks finish higher as techs sizzle again.

text.p: Wall Street stocks bounded higher for the second straight session, as investors raced to acquire the biggest names in technology before year end.
The Dow industrials rose 38 points to close unofficially at 6347. Once again, International Business Machines Corp led the blue chips, surging 6-7/8 to 158-3/4.
"Stocks are in a year-end window-dressing rally and IBM is the one all the money managers want in their portfolios," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
IBM's gains contributed more than half the Dow's advance.
Analysts said the market was showing some early signs of the so-called Santa Claus rally, the late December advance that stocks enjoy nearly every year.
"My suspicion is that we're looking at the early part of it," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "This is a classic time of year when the market has an upside bias."
While the Dow's advance was in line with that tallied in the previous session, the market rally broadened considerably compared with yesterday's session.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a five-to-three margin on the New York Stock Exchange on heavy volume of about 503 million shares.

However, until the market steers clear of the late year portfolio shifting and the spectre of Friday's triple-witching expiration of futures, index options and stock options, analysts said a sustained rally of substance was unlikely.
"Is this the start of a new breakout? Probably not," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.

"I wouldn't read too much into it because it's hard to distinguish what's going on in the last days of a year and it's an options expirations week," he said. "Plus, interest rates are still high and that's a challenge for stocks."
U.S. Treasuries extended their recent slide, with the benchmark 30-year bond falling 1/2 point, pushing the yield up to 6.70 percent.
"This can't go on forever," said Barthel. "There's a very good correlation that says when interest rates go up, the market pays the penalty."

For investors in technology shares, interest rates seemed little more than a footnote, however. The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite jumped about 19 points on the session to 1285, paced by some familiar names. Intel Corp jumped 5-3/4 to 135-3/4 and Microsoft Corp climbed 2-3/4 to 82-5/8.
Compaq Computer Corp raced higher, adding 6-1/2 to 78-3/4 after SoundView Financial raised its near-term rating on the shares to buy from hold.
Shares in the largest drug companies also performed well, with Pfizer Inc up 5/8 to 81-3/8 and Johnson & Johnson up 1/2 to 49-1/8.
Warner-Lambert Co rose 3/8 to 74-5/8 after the company announced it won Food and Drug Administration marketing approval for its cholesterol-cutting drug Lipitor.
Merck & Co Inc gained 5/8 to 76-7/8 after announcing it expected its fourth quarter and 1997 earnings to be at the high end of Wall Street's estimates.

Genetics Institute Inc soared 22-3/4 to 84-1/2 after American Home Products Corp announced it would exercise its option to buy the 40 percent of Genetics Institute it does not already own for $85 per share. Shares in American Home Products fell 1/8 to 59-1/8.

ADT Ltd rose 3-1/8 to 23-1/4 after Western Resources Inc extended an unsolicited $3.5 billion offer to buy the company. Analysts called the bid, which values ADT at 22-1/2 per share, a low-ball offer that was likely to be raised.
The S&P 500 rose 5.50 to 731.54.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
